"revision_justification": "This amendment updates the focal research case, sampling frame, data collection procedures, observation units, and longitudinal observation protocol.

The original registration specified the Life Science Knowledge Workflow represented by WorkflowHub record 2347, version 2, as its focal case. Following further examination of the relevant public scholarly infrastructure records, the amended study focuses on the NEXUS CORTEX Research Workflows project (WorkflowHub Project 490), which contains two repository-specific workflow lineages associated with welcome-to-github and zero-entropy-lab.

The two focal workflow records are:

- WorkflowHub record 2332, version 9, associated with welcome-to-github.
- WorkflowHub record 2334, version 9, associated with zero-entropy-lab.

These records belong to the same WorkflowHub project while preserving distinct source repositories, workflow identities, version histories, source revisions, and provenance relationships.

The revised research design treats the two workflow lineages as a predefined paired set of embedded components within one bounded project-level case. They are not treated as two independent research studies, independent project-level cases, or independent statistical populations.

The eight predefined scholarly-infrastructure layers remain unchanged. The amendment clarifies the project-level sampling frame, the two lineage-specific identity anchors, source-version reconciliation, endpoint selection, evidence-retention procedures, observation units, and repeated observation-cycle protocol.

The observation protocol does not impose fixed calendar dates, predetermined intervals, or a predetermined number of observation waves. Each complete observation cycle applies the same predefined collection and verification procedures to both workflow lineages across all eight infrastructure layers. Actual retrieval timestamps, observation-cycle boundaries, and reasons for initiating each cycle will be retained.

The original WorkflowHub record 2347 and its historical observations remain identifiable as part of the original registration history. They will not be retrospectively rewritten, reclassified, or included as primary observations of the amended focal case.

Historical evidence associated with the two NEXUS CORTEX workflow lineages will also remain distinguishable from the prospective observations collected under the amended protocol.

The amendment introduces no experimental intervention, causal interpretation, population-level generalization, or inferential statistical model. Its purpose is to establish a consistent, reproducible, and auditable research contract for observing the two predefined workflow lineages within their shared scholarly-infrastructure project.1. "344-40": "This study uses a prospective longitudinal single-case embedded observational design with two predefined paired workflow lineages maintained within one shared scholarly-infrastructure project.

THE PROJECT-LEVEL RESEARCH CASE

NEXUS CORTEX Research Workflows

WorkflowHub Project ID: 490

Project record:
https://workflowhub.org/projects/490

The project contains two predefined focal workflow lineages.

LINEAGE A — welcome-to-github

Source repository:
https://github.com/lostlight530/welcome-to-github

WorkflowHub Record ID: 2332

Registered version: 9

DOI: 10.48546/workflowhub.workflow.2332.9

Registered workflow source commit:
1c71b0d983021fd8fbcf6cc8cd2ccbbe7d0d6d2a

LINEAGE B — zero-entropy-lab

Source repository:
https://github.com/lostlight530/zero-entropy-lab

WorkflowHub Record ID: 2334

Registered version: 9

DOI: 10.48546/workflowhub.workflow.2334.9

Registered workflow source commit:
5b360ed531812107cdd8fc1d26c808dcb393a4b8

The two version-specific WorkflowHub records and their associated source commits provide the historical identity anchors for the two workflow lineages.

They do not restrict subsequent observations to those historical source revisions. Later commits, releases, workflow versions, metadata changes, and execution records will be recorded as subsequent states while preserving the original registered anchors.

The two workflow lineages are treated as paired embedded components of one project-level case.

They are not independent project-level cases, independent research studies, or independent statistical populations.

Their shared WorkflowHub project membership provides a common project-level context but does not imply identical source code, identical workflow versions, interchangeable repository histories, or equivalent operational behavior.

Each lineage retains its own source repository identity, WorkflowHub record, DOI, version history, source revisions, execution evidence, and provenance relationships.

THE EIGHT SCHOLARLY-INFRASTRUCTURE LAYERS

The study examines the project and its two embedded workflow lineages across eight predefined scholarly-infrastructure layers.

L1. Source repository

GitHub repositories, workflow source files, workflow definitions, relevant commits, releases, tags, source revisions, and repository-level provenance.

L2. Workflow registry

WorkflowHub Project 490, workflow records 2332 and 2334, their respective version histories, persistent identifiers, source references, creator information, and registered metadata.

L3. Archival repository

Zenodo archival records and concept/version DOI relationships directly associated with either focal workflow lineage. Candidate records must be independently verified rather than assumed.

L4. Identifier registration and resolution

DataCite metadata records, DOI registration agency information, DOI resolution services, and explicit related-identifier relationships for identifiers verified as relevant to either workflow lineage.

L5. Source preservation

Software Heritage origin, visit, snapshot, and preservation representations associated with the two source repositories.

L6. Testing, monitoring, and execution evidence

WorkflowHub-displayed testing metadata, GitHub Actions workflow execution records and associated lifecycle receipts or artifacts, and directly associated LifeMonitor or OpenEBench records where an explicit relationship can be established.

Testing metadata, monitoring states, actual workflow execution records, and execution conclusions will be distinguished.

L7. Researcher attribution

ORCID researcher-work records, WorkflowHub creator information, and associated attribution relationships where direct identifiers or documented source assertions establish a relationship to the relevant project or workflow lineage.

L8. Scholarly discovery and aggregation

OpenAIRE, OpenAlex, Research Software Directory, and nfdi.software records where exact identifiers or documented provenance relationships establish a relationship to the project or either workflow lineage.

The eight layers are functional analytical dimensions rather than mutually exclusive platform categories.

A single infrastructure service may contribute evidence to multiple layers when it exposes distinct functions or records.

The same underlying record will not be counted as multiple independent research objects or independent confirmations merely because it appears in multiple analytical layers.

OBSERVATION DESIGN

The prospective component uses repeated complete observation cycles rather than a predetermined number of calendar-based observation waves.

A complete observation cycle is defined as one full application of the registered endpoint manifest, collection procedures, and verification rules to both workflow lineages across all eight infrastructure layers.

The primary project-level analytical unit is:

One focal project × one infrastructure layer × one complete observation cycle.

Each complete observation cycle therefore contains:

1 project × 8 infrastructure layers = 8 project-layer-cycle observation bundles.

Within these bundles, the two workflow lineages are examined separately.

The corresponding nested lineage-level evidence coverage is:

2 workflow lineages × 8 infrastructure layers = 16 lineage-layer-cycle evidence bundles per complete observation cycle.

The project-level and lineage-level bundles describe different analytical levels. They are not independent statistical samples.

Shared project-level records will be retained once as shared evidence and linked to the relevant lineage-specific analyses without duplication.

Multiple platform endpoints, records, identifiers, API requests, source files, and execution receipts within one observation bundle are nested evidence checks. They will not be treated as additional primary analytical units.

The number of completed observation cycles is not fixed in advance. No predetermined calendar interval, maximum observation-wave count, or fixed calendar end date is imposed.

Each cycle will retain its actual initiation reason, retrieval timestamps, source revisions, endpoint outcomes, and completion status.

The same predefined collection and verification procedures will be applied throughout the study.

The primary comparison will examine each lineage separately and compare their observed metadata, identity, version relationships, provenance, implementation evidence, infrastructure representation, execution records, and state transitions within their shared project context.

DISTINCTION BETWEEN RESEARCH STATES

The study will distinguish:

- Project membership.
- Workflow registry identity.
- Source repository identity.
- Registered workflow version.
- Current repository workflow-file state.
- Source-version relationships.
- Archival availability.
- Identifier registration and resolution.
- Source preservation.
- Testing and monitoring.
- Actual workflow execution evidence.
- Researcher attribution.
- Scholarly discovery and aggregation.

These states will not be treated as interchangeable.

In particular, a WorkflowHub version record does not establish that its registered source commit is identical to the latest source repository state.

A registered workflow does not establish that the workflow was executed by WorkflowHub.

A successful GitHub Actions execution must be interpreted according to its actual workflow identity, run identifier, triggering event, source revision, status, conclusion, and associated execution evidence.

Unrelated repository workflows, including CodeQL executions, will not be classified as NEXUS CORTEX lifecycle executions merely because they belong to the same repository.

HISTORICAL BOUNDARIES

The original focal WorkflowHub record 2347, version 2, is retained as historical registration context.

Its previous observations will not be retrospectively reclassified as observations of the two amended focal lineages.

The historical Brain Evolution record 2337 may be retained as contextual evidence of the earlier welcome-to-github workflow lineage only where a direct provenance relationship is established.

It is not a third primary workflow lineage.

Historical evidence, pre-amendment observations, and prospective observations will remain separately identifiable.

RESEARCH SCOPE

The study is descriptive and does not estimate causal effects, population-level prevalence, institutional adoption, or scientific validity.

No infrastructure will be experimentally manipulated.

No repository, registration, metadata, archival, or monitoring records will be modified by the study.

The study examines publicly observable scholarly-infrastructure representations and their evidence-supported relationships, not the presumed completeness or authority of any single platform.",

The two focal lineages are:

1. welcome-to-github, WorkflowHub record 2332.
2. zero-entropy-lab, WorkflowHub record 2334.

The project-level case and the two embedded workflow lineages constitute the complete primary research sample.

The eight predefined scholarly-infrastructure layers remain fixed.

1 project × 8 infrastructure layers = 8 project-layer-cycle observation bundles.

Within these bundles, the two workflow lineages are measured separately:

2 workflow lineages × 8 infrastructure layers = 16 nested lineage-layer-cycle evidence bundles.

Multiple endpoint queries, records, identifiers, API requests, source revisions, and execution receipts within each observation bundle remain nested evidence checks.

Shared project-level records will be retained once and will not be duplicated as independent underlying records or independent confirmations.

Missing, inaccessible, rate-limited, unresolved, partially verified, incomplete, or failed observations will remain in the observation ledger.

The number of completed observation cycles and the corresponding accumulated observation coverage will be reported explicitly in the final analysis.",

"344-55": "Prospective data collection will begin after submission of this OSF amendment.

The study does not impose a fixed calendar start date beyond the amendment submission boundary, a predetermined interval between observation cycles, a predetermined number of observation waves, or a fixed calendar end date.

An observation cycle may be initiated when a relevant public infrastructure event is identified or when a documented full-scope research review is undertaken.

Relevant events may include:

- A new or modified source commit affecting either NEXUS CORTEX workflow.
- A new repository release or workflow version.
- A WorkflowHub record, version, or project metadata change.
- A newly identified or modified archival record.
- A DOI registration, resolution, or related-identifier change.
- A Software Heritage visit or snapshot change.
- A new relevant GitHub Actions lifecycle execution.
- A change in testing or monitoring representation.
- A relevant researcher attribution or scholarly discovery change.
- A documented full-scope observation review.

The reason for initiating each observation cycle will be recorded before the collection process begins.

Every initiated cycle must apply the registered endpoint manifest and collection procedures to both workflow lineages across all eight infrastructure layers.

A complete cycle requires a documented collection attempt for every predefined endpoint or an explicit record explaining why an endpoint could not be attempted.

Endpoint inaccessibility, rate limiting, missing records, unresolved relationships, or unsuccessful retrievals will not prevent the cycle from being completed and will not be converted into evidence of global absence.

For transient HTTP 5xx responses, timeouts, or rate limits, at most one standardized retry will be performed within the relevant collection attempt. Where a platform provides a Retry-After instruction, it will be respected.

The study has no predetermined maximum number of observation cycles.

Prospective collection will end when the research data-collection phase is formally closed and the closure decision is documented.

Closure will not be determined by whether observations are favorable, unfavorable, statistically significant, or consistent with an anticipated result.

Any observation cycle already initiated before formal closure will be completed where possible. If completion is impossible, its partial status and the reason for incompleteness will be retained explicitly.
